description:
S'mores ice cream is always a winner but as always, I wanted to do it a little differently. 
The poll went up and plenty of folk voted which was AMAZING. S'mores ice cream won out and here we are. 

S'mores (if you aren't aware) are toasted marshmallow and chocolate, sandwiched between graham crackers. As I can't get Graham crackers, I used digestive biscuits, whilst not the same, are reasonably close. 

What made this s'mores ice cream different is the toasting of the marshmallow WITHIN the tub itself. I should have gone bigger with the fire but am selling the house and didn't want to burn it to the ground 😂

So what do you need to make this AMAZING S'mores ice cream?

The ice cream:
500g Milk (I used 1.8% milk)
350g Cream (I used 50% fat Double Cream)
140g sugar
50g dextrose
60g SMP
10g malt extract
5g Triple fold vanilla extract or 10g of normal shop bought extract

Graham crackers 
Chocolate

For the Marshmallow Fluff:
Egg Whites x3 
150g Sugar
50g Golden syrup or Corn syrup (not high fructose)
Pinch of Salt
3-5g Vanilla Extract

Overall, this is one of the BEST ice cream combos i've made. The toastyness, the malt, the buttery crumb..........Sorry, got a bit carried away.

comments.text: Hi :) I'm trying to figure out ice cream stabilizers and you mentioned a proprietary ice cream stabilizer that you added into a bit of sugar to remove lumps from it. I'd really like to try out this recipe...if I were to use Xanthan Gum, I am guessing that I'd make the base and add the Xanthan Gum as stabilizer AFTER the heating process just before I begin the cooling process. Do I have this correct? And I'd be adding 0.1% of the weight of the base in Xanthan Gum. Would I need to mix the Xanthan Gum into some sugar to remove lumps before adding to the base? Are there any other tips that you might suggest?
comments.author: @kateingham9950

comments.text:
Hi, yes Xanthan gum is best incorporated after the heating phase, so once you’ve taken it off the heat is fine. 
Yes it’s always best to mix the stabilizer with a little sugar to make sure it does clump in the liquid and 5g of sugar is enough to do this. Once you’ve mixed it in and start to cool the base, whisk the base a few times in the following hour to make sure the xanthan is fully incorporated.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery
